prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Baytown, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1450; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep it to my first name for now, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving through the intersection in Baytown, heading east on the main road. The light had been green for me, or at least I thought it was.

Q: What happened next?

A: A vehicle coming from the cross street on my right came through the intersection and hit the passenger side of my car. I saw it at the last second and tried to brake, but there wasn't time.

Q: Were you able to stop your vehicle, or did it move after impact?

A: My car spun partway around and ended up against the curb. The airbags didn't go off, but the impact threw me sideways against the door.

Q: Did you feel any injuries right away?

A: Not immediately. I was sore that evening, mostly in my neck and lower back. By the next morning it was worse, with stiffness when I turn my head and a dull ache across my lower back.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the following day and was diagnosed with neck and back strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: Did you have any prior problems with your neck or back?

A: Nothing serious. I had occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that stopped me from working or driving.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping because of the pain, and I'd like the claim to reflect that.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
